Name: Establishing a citywide collective bargaining assessment committee for the purpose of evaluating the City’s collective bargaining practices.
Title: A Local Law to amend the administrative code of the city of New York, in relation to establishing a citywide collective bargaining assessment committee for the purpose of evaluating the City’s collective bargaining practices
BodyName: Committee on Civil Service and Labor

History.Description: This Introduction was Introduced by Council
This Introduction was Referred to Comm by Council to the Committee on Civil Service and Labor

Summary: This bill would create a Citywide Collective Bargaining Assessment Committee to evaluate the collective bargaining practices that are used in negotiations between the City and bargaining units representing municipal employees. The committee would be comprised of representatives from the Office of Labor Relations, the Department of Citywide Administrative Services, the Office of Management and Budget, the Mayor’s Office of Equity and Racial Justice, the Municipal Labor Committee, City Council, and an individual with expertise in labor relations, to be appointed by the mayor. The committee would convene annually to evaluate and issue recommendations on the collective bargaining practices used to determine the terms and conditions of employment for the lowest-paid titles represented in the collective bargaining agreements that are set to expire in the approaching fiscal year, or which have already expired and for which negotiations are ongoing.
Text:
A Local Law to amend the administrative code of the city of New York, in relation to establishing a citywide collective bargaining assessment committee for the purpose of evaluating the City’s collective bargaining practices

Be it enacted by the Council as follows:


Section 1. Subchapter 6 of chapter 1 of title 3 of the administrative code of the city of New York is amended by adding a new section 1-363 to read as follows:
§ 1-363 a. Definitions. As used in this section, the following terms have the following meanings: 
Committee. The term “committee” means the citywide collective bargaining assessment committee. 
Covered collective bargaining agreements. The term “covered collective bargaining agreements” means any collective bargaining agreement that is set to expire during the coming fiscal year, or that have already expired. 
b. Annual Evaluation. There shall be a committee created to conduct an annual evaluation of collective bargaining practices and methodologies that determine the terms and conditions of employment for titles included in covered collective bargaining agreements.
c. Composition. The committee shall consist of 7 members, as follows:  
1. The commissioner of the office of labor relations, or the commissioner’s designee; 
2. The commissioner of the department of citywide administrative services, or the commissioner’s designee; 
3. The director of management and budget, or the director’s designee; 
4. The commissioner of the office of equity and racial justice, or the commissioner’s designee; 
5. The speaker of the council, or the speaker’s designee;
6. A representative from the municipal labor committee; and
7. An individual with expertise in labor relations, to be appointed by the mayor.
d. Evaluation. No later than January 1, and annually thereafter, the committee shall convene to identify and evaluate civil service titles within covered collective bargaining agreements that represent the lowest paid quarter of the municipal workforce. The committee shall consider historic wages, current job responsibilities of such titles, vacancy and attrition rates of such titles, and the true cost of living as part of its evaluation and use such data to inform discussions on how the current collective bargaining practices and methodologies impact the likelihood of such titles receiving substantial pay increases. Such evaluation shall include full-time and part-time titles.
e. Recommendations. No later than April 30, and annually thereafter, the committee shall, in consultation with any stakeholders deemed relevant, make public recommendations for adjustments to collective bargaining practices and methodologies for a minimum of three titles per year. The committee shall submit such recommendations to the mayor, the speaker of the council, the commissioner of the office of labor relations, the director of management and budget, and all collective bargaining units that negotiate with the city.
§ 2. This local law takes effect 60 days after it becomes law.
